ImageDescription.value: Nykyään Rauhanasemana tunnettu puutalo rakennettiin alunperin vuonna 1915 Vammeljoen rautatieasemaksi Kannakselle. Talo siirrettiin Pasilaan 1920-luvulla. ObjectName.value: Svenska Österbotten 2026 språkstatus eller minst 400 svenskspråkiga, södra Finland

Categories.value: Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike missing SDC copyright status|Self-published work|Maps of Ostrobothnia|Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 4.0 missing SDC copyright license|Self-published work missing SDC copyright license|SVG maps of municipalities of Finland|Unspec SVG created with Python|Language-neutral linguistic maps of the Swedish language|Swedish language in Finland|Linguistic maps of Finland Swedish

ImageDescription.value:
Map of the southern half of Finland showing Swedish-speaking Ostrobothnia (Svenska Österbotten) as part of Swedish-speaking Finland, by the official language status of municipalities, supplemented with municipalities that have a sizeable Swedish-speaking minority in absolute numbers. Municipal division as of 2026.
  • Red: the 14 bilingual municipalities of Swedish-speaking Ostrobothnia under Government Decree 1385/2022: Kaskinen, Kristinestad, Närpes, Korsnäs, Malax, Vaasa, Korsholm, Vörå, Nykarleby, Jakobstad, Pedersöre, Larsmo, Kronoby and Kokkola.
  • Grey: the other bilingual municipalities in Åboland, Uusimaa and Kymenlaakso under the same decree, and the 16 municipalities of Åland, which are monolingually Swedish under the Act on the Autonomy of Åland.
  • Light grey: Finnish-speaking municipalities with at least 400 Swedish-speaking residents on 31 December 2025 according to Statistics Finland: Hyvinkää, Järvenpää, Kaarina, Kerava, Kotka, Lahti, Nurmijärvi, Oulu, Pori, Salo, Tampere, Tuusula and Vihti.
The Swedish names of the municipalities are included as tooltips in the SVG file.
